name: 2.5D Parallax Animation
visualIdentity: Separates flat artwork into foreground, midground, and background layers with plausible depth and occlusion. Restrained relative movement suggests depth; it does not establish full 3D modeling. Source artwork retains its colors.
suitableUses: Explicitly suited to layered illustration, paper craft, collage, dioramas, miniature sets, and constrained isometric scenes. Storybook plates suit narrative explainers and children’s stories; period photo cutouts suit historical documentaries when authentic assets exist. Chaptered parallax or scroll storytelling may suit coherent explanatory narratives (inferred).
limitations: Avoid reversed depth motion, excessive separation, exposed layer edges, broken ground contact, or obscured labels. Preserve projection in isometric scenes; camera tilt may alter it. Omit or adapt when artwork is not layered, transitions disrupt continuity, or depth reduces readability. Parallax alone is not full 3D.
palette: No intrinsic palette is specified. Preserve source layer colors and exact task, brand, or reference colors and their roles. Optional fallback tokens for new presentation elements only: background #EFE7D6, foreground #34473F, accent #8A9C85. Use discrete colors; gradients are disabled. Accent with foreground text fails the stated 4.5 normal-text contrast target; verify all actual composited pairings.
motionAndInteraction: Use a shared camera transform with measured, bounded per-layer offsets, generous crop overscan, and deterministic time. For interactive HTML, normalized pointer motion may drive subtle offsets and settle to neutral; scroll may coordinate narrative states or chapter handoffs. Keep labels readable and reverse/direct seeks coherent. Any creature hop is optional and requires suitable assets and a deliberate flick cue. Video must use composition time, never live input.
audio: No fixed soundtrack or mandatory audio layer is specified. Choose music, voice, effects, ambience, or silence for the subject and audience; respect supplied requirements, leave room for speech and reading, and synchronize and inspect the final mix.
assetRequirements: Requires prepared, clearly named layered PNG/SVG artwork or numbered frames with transparency and consistent dimensions. Preserve crop margins and inspect occlusion. Cropping can frame already-separated layers but cannot separate depth, remove backgrounds, or reconstruct hidden artwork. Do not invent archival assets.
combinations: Storybook scene plates or authentic period-photo cutouts are suggested artwork pairings; keep overscan, palette rules, consistent grain where relevant, and modest parallax. Scroll-driven chapter transitions and storytelling are optional orchestration patterns, not inherent style requirements. Choose one compatible handoff and preserve reading order.
productionApproach: Select visual renderer and motion engine by style, assets, action, and fidelity; PixiJS is optional for 2D sprites and layers, Three.js only if genuine 3D is needed. Give each animated property one owner and make state seekable. HyperFrames is the primary composition/export pipeline; use Remotion only if unavailable or a verified limitation blocks a required capability, recording the reason. The pipeline handles assembly, timing, sync, validation, and export, not visual construction. Audio is selected separately. Inspect representative frames and decoded output.
